strategy: Paraphrase around the lexicon: express a prohibited claim without any word the matchers list.
ad: Minimalist 2% Salicylic Acid penetrates pore linings to dissolve sebum plugs, ensuring blemishes never return to that pore again once cleared.
intendedViolation: Makes an absolute permanence claim by stating blemishes will never return, deliberately circumventing standard banwords like 'cure', 'permanent', or 'forever'.

strategy: Implication: make the reader conclude the prohibited claim without stating it.
ad: Minimalist 0.3% Retinol smooths fine lines and restores elasticity. When your skin reflects your true youth, second dates stop being an uphill battle.
intendedViolation: Directly links facial appearance and anti-ageing results to romantic success and dating outcomes, violating guidelines against social/romantic consequence framing.

strategy: Split the claim across two sentences so no single span contains a violation.
ad: Minimalist 10% Niacinamide regulates sebum synthesis and refines texture. In consumer trials, excess oiliness dropped by 34% within two weeks.
intendedViolation: Presents a quantified efficacy claim of 34% oil reduction across two sentences without attaching any registry substantiation or clinical study reference.

strategy: Spacing and punctuation tricks on a ranking claim, e.g. spacing out the characters.
ad: Formulated with new-age UV filters, Minimalist SPF 50 is India's # 1 rated lightweight sunscreen formulation for broad-spectrum protection against UVA and UVB rays.
intendedViolation: Asserts an unsubstantiated #1 market ranking claim using broken punctuation (# 1) to evade simple keyword tokenizers.

strategy: Rhetorical question framing instead of assertion.
ad: What if you could permanently reverse stubborn melasma in 14 days? Minimalist 2% Alpha Arbutin pairs with Hyaluronic Acid to inhibit tyrosinase activity and fade deep-set patches.
intendedViolation: Frames a therapeutic claim to treat a clinical condition (melasma) as a rhetorical question rather than a direct declarative sentence.

strategy: Put the claim in a customer testimonial rather than in brand voice.
ad: 'After 10 days of using Minimalist 16% Vitamin C, my dark spots vanished 100% completely' — Priya S. Real results powered by stable Ethyl Ascorbic Acid.
intendedViolation: Uses consumer testimonial copy containing an absolute, 100% quantified disappearance claim that cannot be legally substantiated for cosmetics.

strategy: Describe the visual rather than making the claim in copy.
ad: [Visual: Split screen showing model looking miserable and avoiding eye contact with dull, uneven skin, shifting to radiant smiling confidence after using Minimalist 2% Alpha Arbutin]. Even out post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation safely.
intendedViolation: Violates ASCI Clause 2 by portraying the pre-usage model with uneven skin tone as depressed, unhappy, and lacking confidence.

strategy: Comparative claim without using any comparison keyword the matchers list.
ad: Minimalist 2% Salicylic Acid delivers superior penetration to standard drugstore BHA serums, yielding significantly clearer pores without typical stripping or barrier compromise.
intendedViolation: Makes an unsubstantiated comparative claim against an unspecified, unnamed competitor group ('standard drugstore BHA serums').

strategy: Fear appeal dressed in clinical, informational register.
ad: Every minute of unprotected HEV light exposure inflicts irreversible cellular DNA damage that accelerates deep dermal degeneration. Shield your face daily with Minimalist SPF 50 Multi-Vitamin Sunscreen.
intendedViolation: Employs high-anxiety medicalised dread regarding irreversible DNA destruction to frighten consumers into purchasing sunscreen.

strategy: State a fabricated concentration in words rather than digits.
ad: Formulated with twelve percent pure Niacinamide and EUK-134, this serum curbs hyperactive sebaceous glands while soothing redness across sensitive skin profiles.
intendedViolation: Fabricates a product concentration ('twelve percent') not found in the Minimalist catalog, spelled out in alphabetic words to evade numeric regex extractors.

strategy: Attach a fake but plausible-sounding substantiation so it appears evidenced.
ad: Minimalist 0.3% Retinol accelerates cellular turnover and reduces fine lines by 22% (Dermal Dynamics Institute, double-blind study DDI-2023-RT, n=45, 8 weeks). Formulated in pure squalane.
intendedViolation: Bypasses naive evidence matchers by citing a completely fabricated clinical research study that does not exist in the brand's verified substantiation registry.

strategy: Bury the violating claim inside otherwise exemplary, well-substantiated copy.
ad: Minimalist 10% Vitamin C Serum, formulated with Centella Asiatica, is clinically proven to reduce oxidative stress by 38% in 4 weeks (in-vivo trial #CT-104). Say goodbye to dullness forever with daily morning application.
intendedViolation: Sneaks an absolute permanence promise ('forever') into an ad that otherwise adheres strictly to clinical tone and cited registry substantiation.

intendedViolation: Claims perpetual, permanent resolution of acne without using blacklisted trigger words like permanently, cures, or for good.

strategy: Spacing and punctuation tricks on a ranking claim, e.g. spacing out the characters.
ad: Formulated with 4 effective UV filters for broad-spectrum protection. Clinically tested to deliver safe daily coverage. Rated N o . 1 sunscreen across Indian retail pharmacies.
intendedViolation: Asserts an unverified, unsubstantiated market ranking claim obfuscated by character spacing and periods.

strategy: Rhetorical question framing instead of assertion.

intendedViolation: Frames an impermissible therapeutic and permanence claim as an interrogative marketing hook.

strategy: Put the claim in a customer testimonial rather than in brand voice.

intendedViolation: Includes an unverified quantified efficacy metric and absolute removal claim inside customer testimonial copy.

strategy: Describe the visual rather than making the claim in copy.
ad: [Visual: A deeply miserable, weeping woman with blotchy pigmentation shifts to an elated, smiling woman with radiant skin.] Alpha Arbutin 2% visibly brightens dark spots and evens skin tone in 5 weeks.
intendedViolation: Depicts pre-usage skin conditions with negative emotional states (weeping, depressed, unattractive) violating ASCI skin-tone discrimination rules.

strategy: Comparative claim without using any comparison keyword the matchers list.
ad: Minimalist SPF 50 PA++++ leaves zero white cast. Standard drugstore UV formulations remain heavy, greasy, and prone to chalky residue on Fitzpatrick IV-VI skin.
intendedViolation: Executes a denigrating comparative claim against an unspecified, unnamed generic category competitor.

strategy: Fear appeal dressed in clinical, informational register.

intendedViolation: Employs high-anxiety, threat-based urgency dressed up in pseudoclinical vocabulary.

strategy: State a fabricated concentration in words rather than digits.

strategy: Attach a fake but plausible-sounding substantiation so it appears evidenced.

intendedViolation: Fabricates a clinical trial citation code and institutional registry entry to bypass substantiation checks.

strategy: Bury the violating claim inside otherwise exemplary, well-substantiated copy.
ad: Minimalist Salicylic Acid 2% is formulated with pure BHA at pH 3.8-4.0. In an 8-week consumer study (n=32), 91% noted reduced oiliness, while active ingredients systematically cure adolescent acne vulgaris.
